# Dillon, New Castle, Williston and Rooks Road · desktop screening

As of 2026-10-19 · Private founder decision memo

## Four sites. One decision rule.

Continue Dillon. Add Rooks Road at equal research priority to today’s leading choices. Screen New Castle and Williston. Stop Adairsville screening. New spending recommendation and authorization in this run: $0.

Rooks Road is Rooks Industrial Gateway at MC-85 and S Rooks Road in Buckeye, Maricopa County, Arizona. The initial offer is about 36 acres, with a separately owned 38-acre expansion advertised. The founder’s ability to visit improves the cost and speed of collecting local facts; it does not establish capacity or approval.

| Site | Research decision | Decisive next proof |
|---|---|---|
| Rooks Industrial Gateway | CONTINUE · DOCUMENTS + LOCAL VISIT | Conflicting broker versions; no APS commitment; current asking price unpublished. |
| Dillon-Baker compartment 53 | CONTINUE · POWER / RU USE / LAYOUT | No exact-load service letter, written RU use path or civil concept layout. |
| New Castle State Road 3 & Riley Road | CONTINUE · TRACT + UTILITY BOUNDARY | 44.35-acre offering / old 49.634-acre legal / 43.55 GIS acres disagree; two utility polygons intersect. |
| Williston Highway 1804 / 48th Street NW | HOLD · EXACT-PARCEL DENIAL | Historic exact-parcel setback failure, no written cure, no power commitment, possible sponsor-scale study costs. |

### The material changes

Williston is materially weaker than its morning listing-only rank: the county denied a setback appeal tied to the exact eastern 76-acre parcel in February 2024. New Castle has a more favorable soil screen, but the matched tax geometry intersects two utility territories. Rooks has inconsistent marketing versions for acreage, building plans and power. Dillon still needs its exact supplier and RU use path.

Hinds 110 remains the existing global founder focus. This four-site work order does not replace that decision or reopen other sites. All four remain research cases, with no validated buyer, no verified available MW and no paid-control clearance.

Deal IDs: Rooks oct19-38995811; Dillon sc-dillon-53; New Castle oct19-27254380; Williston oct19-3934635. Private internal screening. Public records are dated evidence, not title, engineering or utility commitments.

## Compare research effort, not imaginary capacity.

What the business might be: identify land where a buyer could lawfully build a data center, resolve the hard questions cheaply, then transfer useful rights and evidence with appropriate professional advice. A buyer pays only if that work saves more time or money than its own land search or another campus. No such premium is established here.

| Working card | Rooks small phase | Dillon / New Castle |
|---|---|---|
| Status | Analyst hypothesis; not buyer validated | Analyst hypothesis; not buyer validated |
| Initial facility load | 5–10 MW | 20–25 MW |
| Expansion | 74-acre land possibility; MW unknown | 50 MW test case; rights / capacity unknown |
| IT load at illustrative PUE 1.2 | 4.2–8.3 MW | 16.7–20.8 MW |
| Common requirements | Low-water design; two physically diverse carrier paths; acceptable reliability, cost and date | Same requirements, with buyer-specific limits still undefined |

The 5–10 MW Rooks case tests whether a smaller project creates a credible route. It is a separate scope, not a way to declare the larger 25 MW requirement passed. Do not split meters or phases to assume regulatory thresholds disappear. No universal MW-per-acre rule was used.

### Suggested next-hour allocation

Give Rooks and New Castle the next documentary work blocks. Continue Dillon’s existing utility / planning / layout questions. Spend only a short written cure check on Williston’s eastern 76 acres before expanding that work. Rooks stays at equal founder-requested research priority; its current price could still make it harder to control than Dillon or New Castle.

| Current state | Bottleneck | Next decision event |
|---|---|---|
| Public screen completed | Issuer documents, offered surveys and a buyer card | Existing documents establish scope, or the question goes to the responsible issuer |
| No new external requests sent | Outreach is not authorized by this screening | Founder can use the prepared drafts |
| Capital HOLD for all four | 16 required proofs incomplete | Concrete funded structure and full gate review before any money |

Neither a success percentage nor a numeric investment score is defensible yet. Conservative/base/upside scores and evidence confidence are left null; the JSON retains all 52 factors and 34 topics with explicit incomplete status. Missing proof never becomes a zero-risk assumption.

## Rooks: a local, smaller-phase test.

| Item | Evidence and implication |
|---|---|
| Initial land | APN 401-87-007B; assessor LAND_SIZE 36 acres; calculated GIS area about 35.26 acres. Recorded owner RTP GP PHASE I LLC. |
| Expansion | APN 401-87-005; 38 record acres / about 37.43 GIS acres; RTP GP PHASE 2 LLC. Same branded project does not mean one signing entity. |
| Present price | CBRE says contact broker. Current ask is unknown. An older flyer asked $12,301,344 for 35.3 acres; it is historical marketing only. |
| Transaction context | Assessor records show $6,665,000 / deed 20250152752 for 007B and $8,276,000 / deed 20260165681 for 005. These entries are not appraisals or today’s asking price. |
| Use / utilities | I-1, APS and City of Buckeye water/sewer are broker statements. Exact zoning, overlays, lawful data-center classification, will-serve, fire flow and utility allocation remain unissued. |

### Resolve the broker-version conflict first

The Showcase-linked 74-acre brochure advertises a 10 MW substation in process for Q1 2027. The six-page brochure linked directly on CBRE’s 36-acre listing does not make that MW/date statement and uses a different warehouse plan. No file date proves which commercial scope supersedes the other. Request the controlling plan and APS writing; do not carry the number into available MW. [AZ1–AZ4]

### What can make it worthwhile

A buyer-accepted 5–10 MW first phase with dry or low-water heat rejection could use less land and power than the earlier 25 MW working screen. Local observation is inexpensive. A credible seller-cooperation or buyer-funded diligence arrangement would be more plausible than assuming cheap control of multimillion-dollar industrial land. Those are hypotheses, not accepted terms.

### What can stop it

No parcel-specific APS commitment; an unaffordable price or exclusivity premium; data-center or accessory-use conflict; water / fire-flow limits; adjacent residential noise constraints; flood / drainage / easement issues; no buyer-compatible diverse fiber. No evidence yet establishes a net contiguous buildable pad or assignment value.

## Rooks: make a visit answer specific questions.

Parcel map: rooks.png (see PDF / evidence package).

Visit from public roads, or enter only with owner/broker permission. Match the north parcel and expansion boundary to the broker’s survey. Photograph access points, gates, drainage channels / culverts, overhead corridors and visible construction with date, location and viewing direction. Record nearby homes and noise sources. Ask which photographed substation is meant by the marketing claim.

Before a dedicated trip, request the current 36-acre price and APS documents. Bring the APN map and note whether frontage / access shown in marketing exists on the ground. A photograph cannot establish a legal access right, reserved MW, carrier diversity or flood status. Keep observations separate from agency or utility determinations.

NWI returned no features in the queried two-parcel envelope. Flood clearance was not obtained: the Assessor Flood service’s queried layer returned a null-geometry county object, unsuitable for a flood-zone intersection. Buckeye planning services required a token, so exact-use interpretation remains a written city question. [AZ4, AZ6, AZ9, G1]

## Dillon: keep 53 primary, keep 48 unpaid.

| Offering | Current ask / advertised gross acres | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 53 · 080-00-00-053 | $696,000 / 60 · $11,600/ac | Primary existing research case |
| 48 · 080-00-00-048 | $438,000 / 36.45 | Physical-layout challenger; about 38.49 calculated GIS ac |
| 1 · 092-00-00-001 | $608,880 / 51.6 | Unpaid alternate; acreage reconciliation required |
| 72 + 721 · 092-00-00-072 | $671,176 / 57.86 and $333,036 / 28.71 | Two offered portions of one parent; do not double count |
| 102 · 092-00-00-102 | $152,000 / 7.61 | Smaller alternate only; no revival of the prior 20–25 MW case |

The live AFM 53 listing still shows 60 acres and $696,000. A fresh county response matches Baker Anne A, deed 492/54 and plat 18/1. The public zoning-point response is RU Rural. These establish a traceable tax parcel and current marketing; they do not establish seller signing authority, legal access or data-center permission. [SC1–SC4]

### The physical concern persists

The approximately 60-acre polygon is long and narrow. Fresh NWI intersection is about 1.13 acres of mapped riverine features. The Oct 8 dominant-soil screen carried forward roughly 25.13 acres somewhat poorly drained and 3.85 acres poorly drained; roughly 48% combined. The 48 challenger had more well-drained mapped soil but about 3.53 mapped NWI acres. These are overlapping screens, not additive exclusions or net pad areas. [G1, G2; Oct 8 Dillon baseline]

### Power and demand remain the first commercial tests

Public electric overlays do not resolve the exact retail supplier. The nearby Carolinas I-95 Super Park’s Duke / cooperative, voltage and utility descriptions apply to that park, not Baker land. Its documented industrial offering is also a substitute that a buyer can evaluate. Syncranicity needs a specific advantage over that alternative, not a proximity narrative. [SC5]

Next: one combined 53/48 document request for surveys, access/easements, existing utility studies and a written county RU-use path. Proceed only with unpaid research; the current power, layout and buyer proof is too weak for an option.

## Dillon: mapped water is only part of the test.

Parcel map: dillon.png (see PDF / evidence package).

### What changed in the policy watch

SC PSC docket 2026-138-E is an open generic large-load proceeding, with workshops listed for October 26–27, 2026. It does not supply an adopted price or a Baker load commitment. H.5286 is a proposed state moratorium bill; the reviewed status did not show enactment. Neither should be transformed into an automatic parcel approval or an active statewide ban. [SC6, SC7]

Current FEMA NFHL retrieval returned 503. Earlier county flood tiles were only a visual proxy. The resulting flood gate stays unresolved. Do not label the roughly 58.9 acres outside mapped NWI as buildable: setbacks, drainage, easements, flood, access and an actual low-water campus layout still need a combined constraints test.

Written county question: for 080-00-00-053 and 048, identify the controlling jurisdiction and adopted RU use classification for a 20–25 MW non-crypto data center, plus generators, batteries, electrical yard and cooling. State approvals, setbacks, noise limits, appeal timing and any current prohibition. The City of Dillon code must not be substituted for county rules. [SC3, SC4]

## New Castle: promising soil, unresolved offering.

| Item | Evidence and implication |
|---|---|
| Live offering | IRMLS 202617663 / 202617664 describes the same 44.35-acre offer at $899,900, about $20,291 per advertised acre. Sewer is listed as None. |
| Tax identity | APN 33-07-27-000-111.001-021; state parcel 330727000111001021; 2025 statewide geometry loaded Aug 14, 2025. |
| Acreage conflict | Prior listing legal description says 49.634 acres; current offer 44.35; matched GIS polygon calculates about 43.55. A reported 5.27-acre earlier sale could explain the first difference, but no current deed / split survey was reviewed. |
| Pin conflict | Listing coordinate is about 2.43 km / 1.51 miles north of the matched polygon centroid (WGS84 geodesic). Constraint calculations use the APN polygon, not that pin. |
| Jurisdiction | Prairie Township tax record; no municipal feature intersected in the 2025 boundary query. Current planning jurisdiction, ETJ and data-center use path still require county / city confirmation. |

The possible split arithmetic is 49.634 − 5.27 = 44.364 acres, close to the advertised 44.35. That is an analyst inference from listing history, not proof that the offered legal description or access survived unchanged. Current owner and seller authority remain unknown. [IN1, IN2]

### The more consequential conflict: utility territory

IURC polygon clips cover roughly 66% of the matched tract with Henry County REMC and 34% with Duke Energy; about 0.26% overlap reflects mapping inconsistency. This does not give a buyer two feeds, utility choice or a capacity allocation. Get a coordinated written determination of the premises and proposed delivery point before selecting a utility path. [IN3]

High-pressure gas, rail and a nearby substation are seller statements. Gas does not establish firm bridge-generation fuel, rail does not establish a usable crossing, and substation proximity does not establish headroom. [IN1]

## New Castle: two maps, two different uncertainties.

Parcel map: newcastle.png (see PDF / evidence package).

USDA dominant-component mapping clips about 40.33 acres / 92.6% as well drained and 3.22 acres / 7.4% as poorly drained hydric Westland. NWI overlaps about 0.07 acres, a narrow riverine feature. Do not add hydric soil and NWI as separate lost acres. Engineered drainage, agricultural tile, bearing conditions, groundwater and current flood status remain unresolved. [G1, G2]

The separate Knightstown I-70 / SR109 technology-park debate is political and competitive context, not this parcel’s approval. Henry County REMC describes its distribution role and Hoosier Energy’s power-agreement role for that other project. A large project’s publicity is neither available MW nor a countywide use determination for State Road 3. [IN4, IN5]

Next packet: post-split legal / survey; owner and authority; title access and easements; written REMC/Duke service-point response; planning use interpretation; water / wastewater / fire flow; two carrier route proposals. Current FEMA query failed, so no flood clearance is claimed.

## Williston: the exact-parcel history changes the answer.

Hold paid pursuit of the eastern 76-acre parcel. Require current written county evidence of a lawful cure before investing in an expanded data-center case.

The morning lead was the Hwy 1804 / 48th Street NW listing group, advertised as 136 acres in 10–76 acre lots. A current 10-acre example is $199,000 / $19,900 per acre. County matching identifies the eastern 76.767 county GIS-acre parcel as 51-154-02-00-35-035, MS16-0029, owned in tax records by BHANVADIA ND DEVCO III LLC. The listing pin lies on a separate western Yellowstone parcel. [ND1, ND2]

| Date / record | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| Jan–Feb 2024 · county staff memo | The 30 MW GoGo proposal on exact parcel 35-035 failed one-mile sensitive-property and three-mile existing-data-center separation tests. Staff would not accept the CUP application; switching cooling did not cure the identified issue. |
| Feb 20, 2024 · commission minutes | Appeal denied 5–0. This is stronger negative evidence than a generic political-risk proxy. |
| Oct 19, 2026 · ordinance-index check | Signed data-center ordinance remains listed. No written subject cure was found. The historical denial is not called a permanent ban. |

The ordinance regulates a broader data-center use, not merely cryptocurrency. Quiet HPC cannot be assumed exempt. Requirements include CUP review, acoustic work, a signed electric power agreement and maintenance / reclamation security. A current county interpretation is the responsible next source. [ND3–ND6]

### Do not confuse the later GoGo approval

A later LU-0073-24 packet concerns a proposed 10-acre site in Section 12, T153N R103W, Hardscrabble Township. It includes an up-to-8 MW interruptible MWEC arrangement. The screened parcel is Section 35, T154N R102W, Judson Township. The later case demonstrates the sort of specific issuer evidence needed; it supplies no permit or power right here. [ND7]

## Williston: separate the owners, land and power rights.

Parcel map: williston.png (see PDF / evidence package).

The two western Yellowstone parcels report 15.0146 and 51.6692 county GIS acres; their combined approximately 66.7 acres match the scale of a separately marketed 67-acre sibling site. This is an identity clue, not a confirmed offered schedule. Do not assign the eastern denial to every western acre, or assume the western offering escapes the same ordinance. [ND1, ND2]

The current broker brochure contains an unfilled MW placeholder. No subject service agreement was recovered. MWEC’s published C4 tariff is a benchmark, not a total delivered-cost quote. The Basin public onboarding one-pager shows funded studies and a $50,000 nonrefundable application stage, with multiyear implementation phases. Confirm the current version and applicability with MWEC; the newer link was behind member login. [ND8, ND9]

That published application fee alone is five times the founder’s $10,000 cumulative all-in soft-control cap. If applicable, a credible sponsor must fund it; shrinking the land lot does not prove an exemption. Oil / pipeline / terminal neighbors also warrant a buyer-specific hazard and Phase I path. NWI returned no features in the covered 76-acre envelope; flood, soil/geotechnical and environmental clearance remain open.

No complete PASS is asserted. Several proof components have authoritative public evidence; the remaining private, professional or scope-specific pieces are material. No available-MW, COD, buyer commitment, assignable control, usable-acre or profit value is invented.

Policy precedence: founder-approved September 8, 2026 policy v2 requires all 16 proofs, conservative score at least 70 and evidence confidence at least 85 before founder review of paid control. Even a passed review authorizes no money automatically. Existing $5,000 learning and $10,000 cumulative all-in soft-control limits for one paid parcel remain controlling.

A complete 52-factor register and 34-topic coverage register are in the JSON. Unresearched components remain NOT_REVIEWED or UNKNOWN. This memo is a targeted desktop screen, not a completed 116-question pre-option clearance. An independent professional red team has not reviewed it.

## Make any control period survive the evidence timeline.

| Scenario | Illustrative cash / condition | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop continuation | New out-of-pocket recommendation $0; historical exposure and remaining budget not reconciled here | Proceed with existing records and document preparation |
| Small paid-control illustration | E.g. $2,000 nonrefundable option + $2,000 counsel + $2,000 survey/civil scope + $2,000 extension + $2,000 contingency = $10,000 | Arithmetic only, not vendor quotes or an affordable package proved for any site; no room for utility security |
| Basin published fee if applicable | $50,000 application stage, before additional study funding or construction | Founder cannot carry it inside the adopted cap; funded sponsor or hold |
| Rooks price sensitivity | Historical multimillion-dollar marketing and transaction records; current ask unknown | Small acreage does not imply inexpensive control |

Worst-loss rule: count nonrefundable premiums, counsel, reports, deposits, extension payments and nonrecoverable travel once, as cumulative exposure. Downside can be the entire funded amount with no assignment. Purchase money, infrastructure, tariffs, deposits, taxes and construction remain unpriced. No assignment premium, profit margin, ROI or takeout probability is established.

### Cheapest proposed structure to discuss, only after evidence improves

Request existing documents and permission for nonintrusive investigation first. An owner-authorized access / information agreement may support early desktop or professional scoping without an option. If control becomes justified, seek a conditional, assignable or nominee-compatible instrument, objective diligence exits, fixed price, defined utility milestones, reliance / sharing rights and affordable extension rights. Local counsel must resolve authority, access, licensing / compensation and transaction triggers.

Draft seller language: “I am evaluating a defined data-center use and will not represent the land as powered. Would you provide the current survey, title and utility file, permit limited investigation, and discuss conditional control only after the issuer evidence supports the scope?” No terms were proposed or accepted in this run.

Stop if the legal use has no documented cure; seller refuses useful access / assignment; essential offsite rights are unavailable; load / carrier timing outruns affordable control; required studies or security lack sponsor funding; or a buyer would choose a better substitute. No paid vendors commissioned. Obtain scoped civil, environmental and local counsel quotes only after the next decisive free documents support proceeding.

### Transferable evidence plan

Keep each offered survey / legal description with its own APNs; store issuer letters with scope/date and sharing terms; separate marketing from capacity. A buyer room should contain the current source ledger, contradictions, parcel map, utility / carrier / planning responses, capital exposure and unresolved questions. Share third-party material only with appropriate rights; do not promise reliance the issuer has not granted.

### What this pass corrected

A ranked listing is not a qualified site. Williston’s later approval belonged to a different township and parcel. New Castle’s listing pin was unsuitable for constraints. Rooks’ directly linked brochure differed from the 74-acre power-marketed version. Dillon’s industrial-neighbor utility facts did not transfer to Baker land. These distinctions should persist in the Deal Desk.

Learning assignment: read the Basin large-load onboarding one-pager [ND8]. Ask: who is the actual applicant, which money is nonrefundable, and can funded rights / studies transfer to the intended buyer? Then apply the same questions to APS, REMC/Duke and Dillon’s eventual supplier.
